audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may be omitted from the owner-earnings capital charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.1 million fiscal-2026 finance-lease principal, equal to 7.1% of the $340.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if finance-lease asset amortization is added back through D&A without deducting finance-lease principal or an equivalent replacement-capex charge; the overstatement then flows through projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Finance lease expenses are recognized on a straight-line basis over the lesser of the useful life of the leased asset or the lease term and the expenses are recognized in Depreciation and amortization in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the $24.1 million payment and that finance-lease amortization is included in D&A. It does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation supplied an offsetting capital charge. A potentially recurring charge equal to 7.1% of anchored OE is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every component of the $464.2 million fiscal-2026 OE calculation, isolate finance-lease amortization and principal, and rerun all scenarios after deducting either recurring finance-lease principal or a normalized replacement-capex equivalent without deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: The September valuation uses a June bridge despite a pending post-year-end acquisition and financing change
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.5 million expected acquisition price; $378.9 million note-redemption outflow funded with revolver borrowings; $75.0 million post-year-end repurchases
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes the earnings perimeter and interest expense, refinancing changes future interest expense and debt context, and repurchases may change cash and the fully diluted share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction is expected to close on August 27, 2026 for a purchase price of approximately $27.5 million, and will be funded with availability under our existing revolving credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The June-to-September mismatch is demonstrated for the note redemption and repurchases, while the acquisition was only expected to close. The transaction amounts are filed, but the record lacks September cash, revolver borrowings, acquired earnings, actual closing information, and an updated share count. These effects may increase or decrease per-share value, so materiality cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the acquisition closing and funding, then build a September 5 pro forma showing cash, revolver debt, redemption premium, post-year-end repurchases, acquired OE, incremental interest expense, and fully diluted shares; rerun the valuation without separately deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: Future remodel spending may exceed the capital burden embedded in the OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Required remodel expenditures would reduce future OE through the capital-expenditure deduction and could also reduce sustainable growth if the spending merely maintains existing traffic and margins.
audit_findings.evidence: The program aims to remodel approximately 60-80 restaurants in fiscal 2027 and then approximately 10% of the restaurant fleet annually.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a forward program of 60–80 fiscal-2027 remodels followed by approximately 10% of the fleet annually, but provides no remodel cost or maintenance-versus-growth allocation. The burden is prospective and therefore cannot presently be quantified from the supplied numbers, but it must be monitored because projections that omit necessary recurring remodel capital would overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain management's expected cost per remodel, landlord contributions, timing, and maintenance-versus-growth classification; incorporate a normalized annual remodel charge into each projected OE scenario and update it as actual fiscal-2027 spending is filed.

audit_findings.title: The tax rate contains a volatile SBC-related windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.3 million fiscal-2026 excess tax benefit, equal to 6.3% of the $340.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring share-price-dependent tax benefit raises net income and therefore OE; if retained in normalization, it also raises projected after-tax OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The change in the effective income tax rate from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2026 is primarily due to excess tax benefits from stock based compensation.
audit_findings.explanation: The $21.3 million benefit is filed and its inclusion in GAAP net income is demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE series removed or normalized it. Its 6.3% scale relative to anchored OE makes the unresolved treatment reasonably capable of materially changing value, although the exact effect on the log-trend anchor requires a rerun.
audit_findings.action: Trace the excess tax benefit through fiscal-2026 OE and the historical normalization, establish a sustainable cash tax rate independent of vesting and exercise windfalls, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios with the normalized tax treatment.

audit_findings.title: The fully diluted share ceiling is not demonstrably a full maximum-vesting denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Any omitted maximum-performance shares or outstanding options increase the fully diluted denominator and reduce intrinsic value per share and the buy-below price without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares that can vest ranges from 0% of target to 200% of target.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates 41.765 million cover shares, 1.1 million restricted awards at target, vesting up to 200% for some awards, and outstanding options, while the valuation uses 43.3 million shares. The denominator already exceeds the cover count by 1.535 million shares, but award-level maximum shares and option count and strike are missing, so neither the remaining dilution nor its materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile from the August 11 cover count to a no-offset ceiling using award-level target and maximum performance shares, service-based awards, and every outstanding option by count and strike; rerun per-share values if the ceiling exceeds 43.3 million.

audit_findings.title: A one-time insurance recovery may remain in normalized OE
audit_findings.mechanism: An unreversed insurance recovery increases net income and historical OE; asymmetric treatment of the recovery and related settlement can raise the normalized anchor, projected OE, and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Fiscal 2026 is also inclusive of an insurance reimbursement related to a one-time settlement of an employment claim in fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that fiscal 2026 includes an insurance reimbursement related to a one-time fiscal-2025 employment settlement, but it does not separately disclose the recovery amount. Fiscal-2026 Litigation & claims, net was a $3.4 million charge and total Other gains and charges was $8.6 million, but those net captions do not bound the gross reimbursement. The possible normalization error is therefore unresolved and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the gross insurance reimbursement and related fiscal-2025 settlement amounts, trace all components of Other gains and charges into every historical OE observation, apply symmetric normalization, and rerun the OE trend and scenarios.
